newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-ROTOR GO TOP IN TIGHT RUSSIAN LEAGUE FINISH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROTOR GO TOP IN TIGHT RUSSIAN LEAGUE FINISH.

text.p: Unfancied Rotor Volgograd took a slim lead in the battle for the Russian league title and set up a nail-biting end to the season with a 1-0 win at Zenit St Petersburg.

With six games left, last season's champions Alania Vladikavkaz are just a point behind in second place and Moscow's big battalions, led by Dynamo and Spartak, are hard on their heels. The top spot has been changing hands regularly.

Rotor will take heart that Saturday's winner against Zenit came from Oleg Veretennikov, the Russian international midfielder whose solo effort at Old Trafford a year ago this week dumped Manchester United out of the UEFA Cup.
He has been searching for form after injury and coach Viktor Prokopenko had banned him from using his left foot.
Alania, who are based in the Caucasus region, needed Murtaz Sheliya's strike six seconds from time on Thursday to keep their challenge alive with a 2-1 win at home against Chernomorets Novorossiisk.
Dynamo and Spartak, respectively two and four points behind Rotor, both won 2-0. Moscow rivals CSKA, six points off the lead, crushed Rostselmash 5-0 in Rostov.
Rotor are alone among the leaders in being untroubled by European commitments this year. Alania and Spartak both face tricky trips to UEFA Cup first-round return legs this week.

Alania, drubbed 7-2 at home by Glasgow Rangers in a European Cup qualifying match last month, go to Belgium with a 2-1 lead over Anderlecht in the UEFA cup. Spartak travel to Denmark with a slim 3-2 advantage over Silkeborg.
Dynamo have an uphill battle to overturn a 3-0 UEFA Cup deficit against Roma in Moscow. Capital sides CSKA and Torpedo both trail 1-0 as they head for Feyenoord and Dynamo Tbilisi respectively.
